text: End of course test, Track 1. Welcome back to 9-5. Here today is Susie Hawley. We're going to chat a bit about the countries that work the longest hours and how this is unhealthy. It's common knowledge that there is a global increase in the number of hours that people are working. So Susie, which countries work the most? It's really hard to say which countries work the most. There is no doubt that there are countries that work more hours than others. South Korea, for example, works very long hours. A couple of years ago, they cut the working week from 68 hours to 52 hours. But it didn't change much because people still spend a lot of time at their desks. And it's still more than the 48 hours a week maximum that the ILO, the International Labour Organization, recommends. Is there an upper limit to how much time people can spend at work in different countries? Well, in many countries like the UK, Brazil or Turkey, there's a weekly limit on working time. But there are also countries that don't have such a limit. Other countries like Mexico also don't have a limit. And Mexico is the country where people spend the most hours at work. They also only get 10 days of holiday a year, which is a very small amount. There is no question, in my opinion, that too much time working can cause a lot of health problems. For example, if you have a desk job, you are sitting down all day. And studies show that working long hours doesn't improve work performance. It increases your stress and makes you feel bad. What happens when we work too much? What does sitting down all day do to your body? It creates long-term problems for your body. You can develop a bad back or neck problems from sitting too much. There are also more serious health problems. Studies show that you are more likely to get heart disease and other illnesses. When you work too much, you also start to make bad decisions, like eating fast food and not exercising. Mental health problems like feeling unhappy are another issue. Not sleeping enough is also a problem, I guess. Absolutely. It's called sleep deprivation and you feel tired all the time. People need to work to pay bills, so they work more and more. But their health suffers. I think people could be more useful if they didn't work long hours. Everyone knows that when you are tired, you are more likely to have an accident. Who's responsibility is this? Good question. Most people think that managers and bosses are responsible, but it's the person's responsibility too. We should all try to avoid working too much and take more time to eat well and do exercise. We will all work better. Thanks Susie. That's all we have time for now, but tune in next week when we'll be talking to another expert.
